references.text: Isaiah prophesies about the Anointed One sent to proclaim good news—the same mission Jesus describes in Luke 4:43, where he says he must preach the kingdom of God also to other cities.
Earlier in the same chapter, Jesus reads from Isaiah and declares that he is anointed to proclaim good news. Verse 43 confirms this mission and extends it to other cities.
The parallel passage in Mark where Jesus says he must go on to the nearby towns to preach there as well, because that is why he has come.
Matthew describes how Jesus traveled throughout Galilee preaching the gospel of the kingdom—a summary of the work Jesus says in Luke 4:43 he was sent to do.
Jesus went around to all the towns and villages, preaching the gospel of the kingdom, showing the fulfillment of his statement in Luke 4:43 that he must preach the kingdom of God to many cities.
John explains that God sent his Son into the world—this 'being sent' corresponds to Jesus' words in Luke 4:43 that he was sent (ἀπεστάλην) to proclaim the kingdom of God.
Jesus says, 'As the Father has sent me, I send you'—the same sending motif found in Luke 4:43, where Jesus says he was sent to preach the kingdom of God.
Luke describes how Jesus then went from town to town and village to village, preaching the gospel of the kingdom of God, as a direct fulfillment of his words in 4:43.
Peter summarizes Jesus' work: God sent his word to the children of Israel and preached peace through Jesus Christ. This reflects Jesus' own statement that he was sent to preach the kingdom of God.
John testifies that the Father has sent the Son as Savior of the world—the same sending motif underlying Jesus' words in Luke 4:43.
Isaiah speaks of the one who brings good news and proclaims peace and salvation—a prophetic background for Jesus' call to preach the kingdom of God to the cities, as he says in Luke 4:43.
